sentences.text: The Temple Mount -LRB- הַר הַבַּיִת , Har HaBáyit , `` Mount of the House -LSB- of God , i.e. the Temple -RSB- '' -RRB- , known to Muslims as the Haram esh-Sharif -LRB- الحرم الشريف , al-Ḥaram al-Šarīf , `` the Noble Sanctuary '' , or الحرم القدسي الشريف , al-Ḥaram al-Qudsī al-Šarīf , `` the Noble Sanctuary of Jerusalem '' -RRB- , a hill located in the Old City of Jerusalem , is one of the most important religious sites in the world .	Jerusalem	Jerusalem	Old City of Jerusalem	Old City of Jerusalem
It has been venerated as a holy site for thousands of years by Judaism , Christianity , and Islam .	Judaism	Judaism	Christianity	Christianity	Islam	Islam

The present site is dominated by three monumental structures from the early Umayyad period : the al-Aqsa Mosque , the Dome of the Rock and the Dome of the Chain , as well as four minarets .	Umayyad period	Umayyad dynasty	al-Aqsa Mosque	al-Aqsa Mosque	Dome of the Rock	Dome of the Rock	Dome of the Chain	Dome of the Chain	four minarets	Minarets of the Temple Mount
Herodian walls and gates with additions dating back to the late Byzantine and early Islamic periods cut through the flanks of the Mount .	Herodian	Herodian dynasty	Byzantine	Byzantine Empire

Currently it can be reached through eleven gates , ten reserved for Muslims and one for non-Muslims , with guard posts of Israeli police in the vicinity of each .	eleven gates	Gates of the Temple Mount	Israeli police	Israeli police
The Temple Mount is the holiest site in Judaism , which regards it as the place where God 's divine presence is manifested more than in any other place .	Judaism	Judaism	divine presence	Shekhinah

According to the rabbinic sages whose debates produced the Talmud , it was from here the world expanded into its present form and where God gathered the dust used to create the first human , Adam .	Talmud	Talmud	Adam	Adam (Bible)

Since at least the first century CE , the site has been associated in Judaism with Mount Moriah -LRB- הַר הַמוריה , Har HaMōriyā -RRB- ; Mount Moriah is the name given by the Hebrew Bible to the location of Abraham 's binding of Isaac , this identification being perpetuated by Jewish and Christian tradition .	Judaism	Judaism	Mount Moriah	Mount Moriah	binding of Isaac	binding of Isaac	Jewish	Jewish legend	Christian tradition	Christian legend	Hebrew Bible	Hebrew Bible
Several passages in the Hebrew Bible indicate that during the time when they were written , the Temple Mount was identified as Mount Zion .	Hebrew Bible	Hebrew Bible	Mount Zion	Mount Zion

The Mount Zion mentioned in the later parts of the Book of Isaiah , in the Book of Psalms , and the First Book of Maccabees -LRB- c. 2nd century BCE -RRB- seems to refer to the top of the hill , generally known as the Temple Mount .	Mount Zion	Mount Zion	Book of Isaiah	Book of Isaiah	Book of Psalms	Book of Psalms	First Book of Maccabees	First Book of Maccabees

According to the Book of Samuel , Mount Zion was the site of the Jebusite fortress called the `` stronghold of Zion '' , but once the First Temple was erected , according to the Bible , at the top of the Eastern Hill -LRB- `` Temple Mount '' -RRB- , the name `` Mount Zion '' migrated there too .	Mount Zion	Mount Zion	Book of Samuel	Book of Samuel	First Temple	Solomon's Temple
The name later migrated for a last time , this time to Jerusalem 's Western Hill .	Jerusalem	Jerusalem	Western Hill	Mount Zion
According to the Bible , both Jewish Temples stood at the Temple Mount , though archaeological evidence only exists for the Second Temple .	Jewish	Jewish legend	Temples	Temple in Jerusalem
However , the identification of Solomon 's Temple with the area of the Temple Mount is widespread .	Solomon	Solomon
According to the Bible the site should function as the center of all national life -- a governmental , judicial and religious center .
During the Second Temple period it functioned also as an economic center .	Second Temple period	Second Temple period

According to Jewish tradition and scripture , the First Temple was built by King Solomon the son of King David in 957 BCE and destroyed by the Babylonians in 586 BCE .	Jewish	Jewish legend	First Temple	Solomon's Temple	Solomon	Solomon	David	David	Babylonians	Babylonians
The second was constructed under the auspices of Zerubbabel in 516 BCE and destroyed by the Roman Empire in 70 CE .	second	Second Temple	Zerubbabel	Zerubbabel	Roman Empire	Roman Empire
In the 2nd century , the site was used for a temple to Jupiter Capitolinus .	Jupiter Capitolinus	Jupiter Capitolinus
It was redeveloped following the Arab conquest .	Arab conquest	Arab conquest of Syria
Jewish tradition maintains it is here a Third and final Temple will also be built .	Jewish	Jewish legend	Third and final Temple	Third Temple
The location is the holiest site in Judaism and is the place Jews turn towards during prayer .	Judaism	Judaism

Due to its extreme sanctity , many Jews will not walk on the Mount itself , to avoid unintentionally entering the area where the Holy of Holies stood , since according to Rabbinical law , some aspect of the divine presence is still present at the site .	divine presence	Shekhinah	Holy of Holies	Holy of Holies
It was from the Holy of Holies that the High Priest communicated directly with God .	Holy of Holies	Holy of Holies
The Temple was of central importance in Jewish worship , in the Tanakh and the Christian Old Testament .	Jewish	Jewish legend	Tanakh	Tanakh
In the New Testament it remains the site of several events in the life of Jesus , and Christian loyalty to it as a focal point remained long after his death .	New Testament	New Testament

After the destruction of the Temple in 70 CE , which came to be regarded by early Christians , as it was by Josephus and the sages of the Jerusalem Talmud , to be a divine act of punishment for the sins of the Jewish people , the Temple Mount lost its significance for Christian worship with the Christians considering it a fulfillment of Christ 's prophecy at , for example , and .	Jerusalem	Jerusalem	Talmud	Talmud	Jewish	Jewish legend	Josephus	Josephus	Jerusalem Talmud	Jerusalem Talmud

It was to this end , proof of a biblical prophecy fulfilled and of Christianity 's victory over Judaism with the New Covenant , that early Christian pilgrims also visited the site .	Judaism	Judaism	Christianity	Christianity	victory	supersessionism	New Covenant	New Covenant

Byzantine Christians , despite some signs of constructive work on the esplanade , generally neglected the Temple Mount , especially when a Jewish attempt to rebuild the Temple was destroyed by the earthquake in 363 .	Byzantine	Byzantine Empire	Jewish	Jewish legend	earthquake in 363	Galilee earthquake of 363

and it became a desolate local rubbish dump , perhaps outside the city limits , as Christian worship in Jerusalem shifted to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre , and Jerusalem 's centrality was replaced by Rome .	Jerusalem	Jerusalem	Church of the Holy Sepulchre	Church of the Holy Sepulchre

Almost immediately after the Muslim conquest of Jerusalem in 638 CE , Caliph ` Omar ibn al Khatab , disgusted by the filth covering the site , had it thoroughly cleaned , and granted Jews access to the site .	Jerusalem	Jerusalem	Muslim conquest of Jerusalem	Muslim conquest of Syria#Capturing Jerusalem
Among Sunni Muslims , the Mount is widely considered the third holiest site in Islam .	Islam	Islam	Sunni	Sunni	the third holiest site in Islam	Holiest sites in Sunni Islam

Revered as the Noble Sanctuary , the location of Muhammad 's journey to Jerusalem and ascent to heaven , the site is also associated with Jewish biblical prophets who are also venerated in Islam .	Jerusalem	Jerusalem	Islam	Islam	Jewish	Jewish legend	Muhammad	Muhammad	journey to Jerusalem and ascent to heaven	Isra and Mi'raj
Muslims preferred to the esplanade as the heart for the Muslim quarter since it had been abandoned by Christians , to avoid disturbing the Christian quarters of Jerusalem .	Jerusalem	Jerusalem
Umayyad Caliphs commissioned the construction of the al-Aqsa Mosque and Dome of the Rock on the site .	al-Aqsa Mosque	al-Aqsa Mosque	Dome of the Rock	Dome of the Rock
The Dome was completed in 692 CE , making it one of the oldest extant Islamic structures in the world .
The Al Aqsa Mosque rests on the far southern side of the Mount , facing Mecca .	Al Aqsa Mosque	Al Aqsa Mosque	Mecca	Mecca
The Dome of the Rock currently sits in the middle , occupying or close to the area where the Holy Temple previously stood .	Dome of the Rock	Dome of the Rock	Holy Temple	Holy Temple
In light of the dual claims of both Judaism and Islam , it is one of the most contested religious sites in the world .	Judaism	Judaism	Islam	Islam
Since the Crusades , the Muslim community of Jerusalem has managed the site as a Waqf , without interruption .	Jerusalem	Jerusalem	Crusades	Crusades	Waqf	Waqf

As the site is part of the Old City , controlled by Israel since 1967 , both Israel and the Palestinian Authority claim sovereignty over it , and it remains a major focal point of the Arab -- Israeli conflict .	Israel	Israel	Palestinian Authority	Palestinian National Authority
In an attempt to keep the status quo , the Israeli government enforces a controversial ban on prayer by non-Muslims .
